sourceDependencyDigests.invalidationRule: before every Step 2 or Step 3 run, verify the exact raw-file set and canonical JSON selection set, recompute each declared digest and require lowercase-hex equality. A missing, extra or mismatched executable dependency or selected semantic registry value invalidates earlier balance results and aborts before scenario execution. Workflow-mirror bytes may advance phase status without changing the candidate; any semantic specification change still requires a new candidateId, candidate digest and Step 1 re-seal

step2ToStep3ExecutableSealContract.sealRawFileRule: the seal must pass validateExecutableSealBytes: one strict JSON object, exactly the required fields in the declared order, two-space indentation, UTF-8 without BOM, one final LF, lowercase SHA-256 fields, no duplicate or extra key, schemaVersion=1 and step2Verdict=PASS

sourceTreeContract.sourcePathRule: each entry is a unique repository-relative POSIX path beneath exactly one fixedSourceRoots directory and names an existing regular non-symlink file; absolute paths, dot or dot-dot segments, backslashes and empty segments are forbidden
sourceTreeContract.coverageRule: immediately before every Step 2 or Step 3 run, recursively enumerate every regular non-symlink file beneath fixedSourceRoots without following directory symlinks and require exact set equality with simulatorSourceFiles; a missing, extra, unreadable, symlinked or non-regular entry aborts
sourceTreeContract.moduleLoadingRule: all simulator entrypoints, static imports and local data dependencies must resolve inside simulatorSourceFiles; dynamic import with a computed specifier, eval, Function construction, native addon loading and execution of unlisted local code are forbidden
sourceTreeContract.externalLocalInputRule: the only readable repository-local inputs outside fixedSourceRoots are candidate-v1.json, run-plan.json, result.schema.json, the Step 2 executable seal, the Step 3 lifecycle ledger and declared result/output files; result validation code and every helper it imports live under fixedSourceRoots and are therefore covered by the tree digest
sourceTreeContract.orderingRule: simulatorSourceFiles is nonempty and strictly ascending by unsigned UTF-8 byte sequence; because sourcePathPattern is ASCII-only this is bytewise ASCII order
sourceTreeContract.entryRule: for each listed path construct exactly the two-element JSON array [path,sha256RawBytesLowercaseHex] in that order
sourceTreeContract.treePreimageRule: construct the JSON array of entries in simulatorSourceFiles order using UTF-8 JSON.stringify with no whitespace, BOM or trailing LF
sourceTreeContract.holdoutSimulatorDigestRule: every Step 3 lifecycle record simulatorRawSha256 equals this seal's simulatorSourceTreeSha256 exactly; simulatorRawSha256 is an alias for the sealed source-tree digest and never a digest of one file

step2ToStep3ExecutableSealContract.creationRule: after Step 2 has one valid PASS verdict, atomically write this seal from the exact executable and result artifacts that produced it; the seal is downstream evidence, not a candidate dependency, so creating it and advancing workflow mirrors do not alter the candidate raw digest
step2ToStep3ExecutableSealContract.step3PreflightRule: before holdout-bank ledger preflight, validate the seal's strict raw bytes and schema, recompute the candidate raw and normalized digests, source-tree digest and count from the sealed run plan, result schema and validator raw digests and exact Node version, then require every value and step2Verdict PASS to match; any missing, extra, reordered, mismatched or invalid value aborts before a holdout draw
step2ToStep3ExecutableSealContract.oneWayAuthorityRule: Step 3 consumes this immutable Step 2 seal; Step 3 output and workflow-mirror changes never rewrite or replace it

calibrationMutationPolicy.pointerMatchRule: encode each existing numeric leaf as RFC-6901 JSON Pointer; an array item pointer includes its decimal index and is eligible only when at least one allowedNumericPointerPatterns regex matches and no immutableNumericPointerPatterns regex matches. Regexes are ECMAScript Unicode-disabled and evaluated exactly as stored. Object keys and array lengths remain immutable, so waves/enemyCount and roster counts are structural and cannot be calibrated
calibrationMutationPolicy.numericDomainClassificationRule: for every existing or mutated numeric leaf that canCalibrate accepts, evaluate calibratableNumericDomainRules in listed order and apply the first matching rule; no allowed numeric leaf may remain unmatched. number means any finite JSON number, integer requires Number.isSafeInteger, bounds are inclusive or exclusive exactly as named, and all values also obey formulaRules.maximumAbsoluteInteger. Domain validation occurs before any Step 2 scenario. String semantics may further make a numeric field immutable; specifically cat.d02.rescued skill.hitCycleLength remains fixed at five until its canonical skill ID and resolution text are separately versioned

nonBindingPriorRangeRules.rule: this pair is an exploration prior only and is not an admissible-value bound; survival acceptance and the numeric domain decide admissibility even outside it

calibrationMutationPolicy.rangeBindingRule: each inclusiveRangeBindings value is calibratable, each range is immutable, both pointers must resolve, the range must contain exactly two finite ascending numbers, and the current or mutated value must stay between them inclusive. nonBindingPriorRangeRules are the only named exceptions and may not be silently promoted to acceptance bounds
calibrationMutationPolicy.immutableRegardlessOfRoot: every string, boolean, null, object key, array length, canonical ID, state-field shape, state transition, formula algorithm/operand, event order, PRNG/schedule/persona procedure, acceptance threshold/statistic procedure, fixedProductContractPointer and schema rule is immutable in Steps 2 and 3
calibrationMutationPolicy.mutationTransaction: each accepted Step 2 numeric change creates a new candidateId and digest and invalidates all earlier Step 2 results. Step 3 starts only from a frozen passing digest and an unobserved holdout bank. One registered immutable-candidate consumption session may finish after its first output spends the bank, but may not mutate the candidate. Once any seed-level or aggregate Step 3 result from that bank is materialized or observed, a later candidate or simulator-semantics change may not reuse that spent bank for promotion: return to Step 1, register a disjoint unobserved bank, re-seal, and rerun all of Step 2 before Step 3. A same-digest rerun is limited to byte-equivalence verification or infrastructure recovery that exposed no result, and never replaces the first valid acceptance verdict. Partial materialization followed by failure spends the bank even when no valid verdict exists

rounding.timeInternalMilliseconds: all clock values, event timestamps, event delays and event durations are integer milliseconds. The legacy-named support.supply-lift deliveryWorkRequiredMs and run.deliveryWorkRemainingMs are the sole exceptions: they are six-decimal work-unit accumulators where one work unit equals one base millisecond, not timestamps or durations
rounding.derivedEventTime: convert seconds to milliseconds where needed, then ceiling to the next clockModel.fixedStepMs boundary; no combat, projectile, heal, decision, transition or re-clear event may resolve earlier than its unquantized time

formulaRules.numericFormulaAuthority: fields named formulaId or ending FormulaId resolve only the sibling and explicit path fields named by each rule; human-readable formula text never overrides those numeric fields, and any number repeated in prose is non-authoritative

primitiveDefinitions.roundHalfUpNonnegative: floor(value + 0.5); every input governed by this candidate is nonnegative
primitiveDefinitions.medianThree: sort the three finite values ascending and select index 1
primitiveDefinitions.invalidArithmetic: a negative base for exponentiation, zero divisor not explicitly guarded, NaN, Infinity, or magnitude above maximumAbsoluteInteger fails the scenario

algorithmDefinitions.minimum-level-and-diminished-excess: minimum(level, effectDiminishingAfterLevel) + maximum(0, level - effectDiminishingAfterLevel) * effectPerLevelMultiplierAfterDiminishing
algorithmDefinitions.floor-ehp-times-ordered-wave-share: roundSixDecimals(floorEhp * waveShare), with the final wave receiving the exact residual floorEhp minus all earlier rounded wave EHP
algorithmDefinitions.normal-interval-divided-by-clamped-simul: normalAttackIntervalMsInitial / clamp(simultaneousAttackerFactorBase + simultaneousAttackerFactorPerAliveEnemy * aliveEnemyCount, simultaneousAttackerFactorBase, simultaneousAttackerFactorMaximum), then apply rounding.derivedEventTime
algorithmDefinitions.reciprocal-of-sum-of-positive-threat-sha: roundSixDecimals(1 / sum(threatShares[bucket] / weapon.attackMultiplierByThreat[bucket] for every bucket whose threatShares[bucket] is positive)); reject a nonpositive multiplier or zero sum
algorithmDefinitions.placement-link-multiplier: require differentAdjacentShopTypeCount, sameAdjacentShopTypeCount and activeSupportLinkCount to be nonnegative safe integers, require differentAdjacentShopTypeCount+sameAdjacentShopTypeCount<=adjacency.maximumLinksPerPlacement and activeSupportLinkCount<=adjacency.maximumSupportLinksPerPlacement, then return roundSixDecimals(1 + differentAdjacentShopTypeCount*adjacency.differentShopTypeBonusPerLink + sameAdjacentShopTypeCount*adjacency.sameShopTypeBonusPerLink + activeSupportLinkCount*adjacency.supportLinkBonusPerLink)
algorithmDefinitions.zero-if-highest-zero-else-clamped-refere: highestReachedFloor <= 0 ? 0 : roundSixDecimals(clamp(reference, roleNeutralReward * uIndex.clampLowerMultiplier, roleNeutralReward * uIndex.clampUpperMultiplier))
algorithmDefinitions.base-seconds-divided-by-clamped-current-: rawSeconds=floorBaseSeconds / clamp(currentEffectivePower / recordedFirstClearEffectivePower, postDawnKnownFloorReclear.powerRatioClamp[0], postDawnKnownFloorReclear.powerRatioClamp[1]); rawMs=rawSeconds*1000; quantizedMs=apply rounding.derivedEventTime to rawMs; return maximum(minimumSecondsPerFloor*1000,quantizedMs)/1000 in seconds
algorithmDefinitions.first-selected-cat-ko-seconds-or-project: if runtime.firstSelectedCatKoMs is a finite nonnegative integer return maximum(decisionPolicies.purchase.ratioEpsilon,runtime.firstSelectedCatKoMs/1000); if it is null return effectComposition.utilityProjectionWindowSeconds+clockModel.fixedStepMs/1000; any other value fails the scenario
algorithmDefinitions.sum-scheduled-heals-divided-by-interval-: roundSixDecimals(sum(scheduledHeals[i] / healIntervals[i] for matching indexes i) * totalHealingMultiplier); reject arrays of different lengths or a nonpositive interval
algorithmDefinitions.sum-build-weight-times-natural-log-posit: sum(buildWeights[category] * log(maximum(categoryAfter[category], ratioEpsilon) / maximum(categoryBefore[category], ratioEpsilon)) for every utility category) / maximum(waitSeconds, minimumUtilityDenominatorSeconds)
algorithmDefinitions.foreground-live-income-over-fixed-step: raw=roundSixDecimals(priorFraction + liveIncomePerSecond * fixedStepMs / 1000); creditedWholeCoins=floor(raw); retainedFraction=roundSixDecimals(raw-creditedWholeCoins); return both values

clockModel.combatResolution: deterministic-fixed-step-individual-actor-atomic-event-model; enemy EHP threat buckets are aggregate accounting only and never pool allied HP or determine clear by projected TTK
clockModel.sameTickStateRule: collect every event whose quantized timestamp equals the current tick, order it with combatRules.simultaneousEventOrder, and commit deltas once
clockModel.foregroundFixedStepIncomeCommitRule: for each complete visible running half-open interval [t-fixedStepMs,t), snapshot the fully committed live-income composition at its left endpoint and evaluate shopModel.liveIncomeAccrual exactly once from that rate. At right endpoint t, credit its whole coins/fraction before collecting or resolving any event in combatRules.simultaneousEventOrder and before any floor clear, phase entry/exit, shop/support/relic mutation, purchase, Dawn, success latch, hide or other boundary at t. Those right-end mutations affect only the next complete interval; t=0 and partial visible intervals accrue zero. A floor-ending or F100-success interval therefore credits its old active composition once before the final combat/boundary transaction, while a phase-three lockdown entered at t first affects [t,t+fixedStepMs). Mandatory decisions, defeat presentation, wave gaps and floor transitions use the same interval rule whenever their own contract permits live income. On hide at t, first commit an otherwise complete visible interval then persist; on return at t never credit background time or a retroactive partial interval
clockModel.persistedStateRevisionRule: system.stateRevision is a nonnegative safe integer. Every successful externally visible persisted transaction—hide pending-event creation, one standalone single-level/bulk purchase commit, complete floor-clear boundary, standalone shop/relic/party/armament/reconfiguration commit, Dawn, or offline settlement—uses compare-and-swap against the revision read at transaction start and writes exactly old+1; failure writes nothing and retries from a fresh load. postClearDraftRevisionRule is the sole exception for subtransactions nested inside one complete post-clear boundary, and offline.settlement.atomicCommitRule is the sole exception for settlement-internal operations: each group exposes only its one final increment. Fixed combat ticks, previews, diagnostics and live-income fractional accrual without persistence do not increment it
clockModel.postClearDraftRevisionRule: when a same-timestamp batch would clear the final wave/phase, begin floorClearCommitOrder with boundaryBaseRevision=system.stateRevision and boundaryBaseGameplay equal to the exact authoritative pre-final-batch state; sameTimestampCombatLimitPreflightRule supplies its fully resolved clone and exactFinalBatchCount without mutating real state. Stage that final combat state, reward, unlocks, required decision, choice, cat/achievement updates, optional reconfiguration, every purchase, elapsed post-clear gameplay clocks and complete U snapshot only in transactionDraft under gameplayExecutionClockRule. Maintain draftEconomyDelta from zero and initialize draftCombatEventDelta=exactFinalBatchCount; those final-batch events, HP/EHP, KOs, objective state, counters, logs, ordinals and post-clear gameplay clock advances remain draft-only, while scenario measurement clocks advance independently and are never transactional. Immediately before staging each counted floor reward, shop placement, reconfiguration, single-level purchase or atomic-bulk purchase, preflight committedEconomyCount+draftEconomyDelta+1 against stopPolicy.maximumEconomyTransactions; a legal unit increments draftEconomyDelta and appends its deterministic before/after log. Before staging supportModel.firstDistrictScriptedDelivery, preflight committedCombatEventCount+draftCombatEventDelta+exactly 3 against stopPolicy.maximumCombatEvents; a legal scripted delivery adds 3 to draftCombatEventDelta and appends all three unique arrival logs. For F1-F99, before every positive-time advance inside the draft, apply stopPolicy.limitBoundaryRule: the complete final boundary CAS is legal when every required suffix action finishes at or before both inclusive time maxima, including zero-time actions at an exact boundary, but if the next required advance or action would occur later, discard the whole draft back to boundaryBaseGameplay, including the final combat batch. Leave system.monotonicClockMs and system.foregroundClockMs at boundaryBaseGameplay but retain the actual elapsed prefix in scenario.resultWallElapsedMs and scenario.resultForegroundElapsedMs, advancing only the applicable result clock or clocks to the earliest exact time maximum; do not expose a gameplay clock, event-queue or counter prefix from the discarded draft. F100 uses stopPolicy.floor100TerminalRule instead and may latch success in its atomic core clear without a post-clear suffix. If either a time boundary, the next economy unit or the scripted combat-event group rejects the draft, discard the entire transactionDraft—including the final combat batch, reward, every prior staged mutation, counter, log, contact and ordinal—leave externally visible gameplay, HP/EHP, event queue and both committed counts at boundaryBaseGameplay, and stop INCOMPLETE_WITH_EXPLICIT_REASON; never persist a final-kill or other prefix, one/two scripted arrivals, or a trimmed purchase loop. Choice contacts and purchaseEvaluationOrdinal changes are staged too; none mutates externally visible run/profile fields or system.stateRevision. With no interruption, persist-complete-post-clear-boundary performs one compare-and-swap requiring current revision=boundaryBaseRevision and writes the entire draft plus committedCombatEventCount=base+draftCombatEventDelta, committedEconomyCount=base+draftEconomyDelta and stateRevision=boundaryBaseRevision+1. If hide interrupts, the one hide CAS separately writes pending.hiddenAtMonotonicMs from the transactionDraft staged clock at the hide timestamp together with the pending event and frozen context, advances system.stateRevision from r to r+1, sets frozenForegroundContext.sourceStateRevision and pending.sourceStateRevision to r+1, and leaves externally visible gameplay run/profile and gameplay clocks at boundaryBaseGameplay; the draft retains boundaryBaseRevision and all internal economy/combat/log/ordinal/clock deltas. Resume requires current revision=context.sourceStateRevision, finishes only inside the same draft, then the final boundary CAS exposes all gameplay deltas and writes exactly current revision+1. A CAS failure exposes none of the draft and reloads or follows interruptionDurablePhaseRule; nested subtransactions never consume additional state revisions

scenarioIdentityBindings.ordinaryReturnSchedule: use its exact active, standard, passive or continuousFirstTen schedule key and instanceKey=base
scenarioIdentityBindings.driftMeasurement: use persona.baseline, scheduleKey=drift and instanceKey=drift; when its F20 clone becomes offline.acceptanceReferenceSnapshot replace the schedule and instance binding before hide
scenarioIdentityBindings.offlineExplicitCase: use persona.baseline, scheduleKey=offlineAcceptance and instanceKey equal to the exact returnSchedules.explicitOfflineCases caseKey
scenarioIdentityBindings.offlineRepeatedIdempotency: use scheduleKey=offlineAcceptance and instanceKey=idempotency; arm one event and retry that same event ID seven times
scenarioIdentityBindings.offlineRepeatedClonedSnapshot: use scheduleKey=offlineAcceptance and instanceKey=cloned-cNN where NN is the one-based cycle ordinal zero-padded to two digits

scenarioIdentityBindings.reclearBandFixture: use persona.baseline and scheduleKey=reclearNormal or reclearBoss. For repeatedCycleCases.idempotency use instanceKey normal-idempotency or boss-idempotency, arm one event and retry that exact event ID seven times. clockModel.saveIdConstruction: initialState.system.saveId is a template sentinel. Before the first event of every simulation scenario replace it with exact ASCII `sim|S`+seed zero-padded to 6 decimal digits+`|B`+build key+`|P`+persona ID+`|R`+one clockModel.simulationScheduleKeys value+`|X`+the lowercase-hyphen instanceKey required by clockModel.scenarioIdentityBindings. Build is combat, reinforcement or commerce and persona is persona.active, persona.baseline or persona.passive. Runtime instead creates once and persists `runtime|` plus 32 lowercase hexadecimal cryptographic-random digits. Every armed saveId must match clockModel.simulationSaveIdRegex; no diagnostic may borrow another schedule label, and no truncation or locale formatting is allowed
clockModel.monotonicClockLifecycle: system.monotonicClockMs starts at 0 and is a persisted nonnegative safe-integer gameplay logical wall clock. In simulation, every successfully committed foreground fixed step, decision, transition and legal offline return advances the active gameplay execution owner's staged copy by its exact legal elapsed milliseconds under gameplayExecutionClockRule; an ordinary successful commit therefore normally follows cumulative schedule time, but a rejected transaction or unsynthesized return leaves the persisted system clock at its last durable boundary while scenario result time continues only under scenarioMeasurementClockRule. At hide, pending.hiddenAtMonotonicMs is the active gameplay execution owner's current staged monotonic value, including a blocking post-clear transactionDraft value that may be later than the externally visible boundary-base system.monotonicClockMs. For authoritative Step 2/3 execution, only when the declared offline return lies at or before the inclusive scenario wall-clock maximum, set injected hiddenAtWallClockUnixMs=scenario.resultWallElapsedMs at the segment start, injected returnWallClockUnixMs=hiddenAtWallClockUnixMs+s*1000, monotonicReturnTimestampMs=hiddenAtMonotonicMs+s*1000, and then stage system.monotonicClockMs at that return value in the active execution owner. The secondary-branch standard-schedule diagnostic is the sole Step 2/3 exception: under diagnosticHorizonClockRule it injects diagnosticWallClockBaseMs+diagnosticElapsedWallMs for hide/return host timestamps and never reads scenario.resultWallElapsedMs. An authoritative return later than the scenario maximum is never synthesized: scenario.resultWallElapsedMs advances only to the exact maximum while hidden, the persisted system.monotonicClockMs remains at the hide boundary, and the pending event/context remains unsettled. Runtime is not subject to the simulation's 30-day stop: runtime hide stores the nonnegative safe-integer host Unix millisecond reading in pending.hiddenAtWallClockUnixMs; return reads host Unix milliseconds once, sets rawElapsedMs=maximum(0,returnWallClockUnixMs-hiddenAtWallClockUnixMs), monotonicReturnTimestampMs=hiddenAtMonotonicMs+rawElapsedMs and monotonicClockMs to that value before the 24-hour reward cap calculation. A host rollback therefore gives zero elapsed and never decreases the logical clock; overflow or non-integer readings fail settlement
clockModel.localClockTrustBoundary: runtime has no trusted server clock and cannot distinguish one legitimate absence from one manually advanced device-clock interval; never claim otherwise. The 24-hour cap bounds one interval. Persist system.lastAcceptedWallClockUnixMs after every settlement. If a later hide or return host timestamp is below that value, mark the pending interval rollbackQuarantined=true, pay zero, keep lastAcceptedWallClockUnixMs unchanged and clear only through the normal idempotent settlement. A later interval becomes eligible only when both hide and return timestamps are at least lastAcceptedWallClockUnixMs. A forward jump followed by rollback therefore cannot be farmed repeatedly below the accepted high-water mark; adding trusted-time enforcement requires a separately approved server contract
clockModel.scenarioMeasurementClockRule: Step 2/3 constructs one simulator-owned non-persisted scenario envelope whose scenario.resultWallElapsedMs and scenario.resultForegroundElapsedMs are nonnegative safe integers initialized exactly from scenarioMeasurementClockInitialState. Advance each exactly once by actual simulated elapsed wall or visible foreground milliseconds, respectively; offline time advances only resultWallElapsedMs. These counters are the sole authoritative operands for maximumWallClockSeconds and maximumForegroundSeconds and never belong to run, profile, system, persistence, stateRevision or compare-and-swap. TransactionDraft, deferred-suffix, settlement or other gameplay rollback never rewinds them: on a time-cap rejection they advance only to the earliest exact inclusive maximum while the gameplay execution owner rolls back to its durable boundary. Non-mutating diagnostic clones under diagnosticHorizonClockRule neither read nor mutate these counters. A successful ordinary gameplay commit normally leaves the active system clocks aligned to the corresponding result clocks, but equality is not required after an atomic rollback, a hidden no-return stop or an unfinished deferred suffix
clockModel.gameplayExecutionClockRule: For gameplay event ordering, timers, command-window phase, persistence and pending-offline anchors, the active execution owner is the innermost transactionDraft or deferred transaction clone when one exists and otherwise the externally visible system state. Read and advance that owner's staged system.monotonicClockMs and system.foregroundClockMs; a successful owner commit publishes both, while rejection discards both back to the last durable boundary without changing scenario measurement clocks. Preserve manualCommandAnchorForegroundMs unless its declared command transaction commits. If hide interrupts a blocking-post-clear-boundary, pending.hiddenAtMonotonicMs is copied from the transactionDraft's staged system.monotonicClockMs at the exact hide timestamp. In authoritative Step 2/3 execution pair it with injected hiddenAtWallClockUnixMs=scenario.resultWallElapsedMs; in the secondary-branch standard-schedule diagnostic pair it instead with diagnosticWallClockBaseMs+diagnosticElapsedWallMs under diagnosticHorizonClockRule. The hide CAS may persist that pending anchor and context only in its execution owner while externally visible gameplay clocks remain at boundaryBaseGameplay
clockModel.diagnosticHorizonClockRule: This rule applies exactly to effectComposition.boundedDecisionProjectionProcedure, dawn.decisionPolicy.projectionProcedure, dawn.branchSpendPolicy.afterPrimaryCapChooseHighestMarginalEffectivePower, dawn.firstReturnToPriorMaximumEvaluationProcedure and acceptance.activeToPassiveThreeMinuteProcedure. Each non-mutating clone retains the source's absolute system.monotonicClockMs, system.foregroundClockMs, system.manualCommandAnchorForegroundMs, system.floorAttemptOrdinal, timers and keyed command-window phase; never reset or overwrite them. Inside each clone those gameplay fields advance normally, while separate clone-local nonnegative safe-integer diagnosticElapsedWallMs=0, diagnosticElapsedForegroundMs=0 and diagnosticAttemptCount=0 measure only that caller's work. At clone creation set immutable diagnosticWallClockBaseMs=maximum(source.system.monotonicClockMs,source.system.lastAcceptedWallClockUnixMs when non-null else 0), require it to be a nonnegative safe integer and use diagnosticWallClockBaseMs+diagnosticElapsedWallMs as the sole injected hide/return host-wall timestamp within the clone. Diagnostic offline settlement computes elapsed from those injected values, compares rollback quarantine only with the clone's high-water mark, and updates pending/high-water state only inside the discarded clone; the authoritative scenario.resultWallElapsedMs and scenario.resultForegroundElapsedMs, source clocks, source attempts, source counters, source pending/high-water state and source gameplay state remain unchanged and are never read as diagnostic elapsed or used to clip the diagnostic. Use the caller's exact horizon as the local inclusive time cap: utility and Dawn projections each run 300000ms wall and foreground, active-to-passive comparison runs 180000ms wall and foreground, the secondary-branch standard schedule runs exactly 86400000ms wall and 720000ms foreground, and first-return runs at most stopPolicy.maximumForegroundSeconds*1000 local wall and foreground milliseconds. Floor-attempt admission compares diagnosticAttemptCount, not the retained source system.floorAttemptOrdinal, with stopPolicy.maximumFloorAttempts; increment both the clone identity ordinal normally and diagnosticAttemptCount once per clone attempt. Economy and combat use the isolated clone-local counters from stopCounterLifecycleRule and their normal maxima; further Dawn remains disabled where the caller declares it. All alternatives from one source share identical absolute source fields, identical diagnosticWallClockBaseMs and zero local counters. dawn.branchSpendPolicy.secondaryBranchEarlyTerminalRule and acceptance.activeToPassiveEarlyTerminalRule are the only cases that pad diagnostic local clocks after an early atomic F100 success while leaving gameplay time, completion metrics and the terminal snapshot frozen. Reaching a caller horizon exactly otherwise resolves that caller's already-due same-timestamp fixed point and is a successful endpoint rather than INCOMPLETE, with one explicit secondary final-return rule: synthesize the standard schedule's final offline return exactly at diagnosticElapsedWallMs=86400000 and permit only its complete zero-positive-time return, settlement, disabled-Dawn checkpoint and context-validation fixed point. If any blocking context requires resumedForegroundMs>0, or pendingOfflineEvent, frozenForegroundContext or transactionDraft remains after that zero-time fixed point, do not extend the wall or foreground horizon, do not score the durable pre-return or partially settled state, preserve the source, and mark only that candidate's marginal score non-finite so secondaryLoopRule rejects it; if every candidate is non-finite the existing loop stops with shards unspent. Other work later than a caller horizon fails or returns positive infinity exactly as that caller declares
clockModel.foregroundProgressionTime: foregroundProgressionSeconds=scenario.resultForegroundElapsedMs/1000 exactly. scenario.resultForegroundElapsedMs advances only by actual visible simulation fixed steps, decisions, defeat presentations and transitions declared as foreground, pauses offline, remains advanced through a discarded gameplay draft, and is the sole authoritative operand for stopPolicy.maximumForegroundSeconds. system.foregroundClockMs is the persisted gameplay and command-phase clock governed by gameplayExecutionClockRule, not the scenario reporting or stop-budget operand
clockModel.touchActiveTime: time with accepted tap, hold, purchase, loadout, or navigation input
clockModel.wallClockElapsedTime: wallClockElapsedSeconds=scenario.resultWallElapsedMs/1000 exactly, including actual foreground, offline and rolled-back terminal elapsed time; system.monotonicClockMs remains the persisted gameplay logical clock and is not the scenario reporting or stop-budget operand

returnSchedules.personaBindingRule: a schedule's personaId is its native stress-run persona; an explicit personas.extremeComparison persona overrides only command and decision behavior while preserving the selected schedule's segment timestamps
returnSchedules.segmentBoundaryRule: the ending timestamp belongs to the following segment, except that a Step 2/3 schedule segment clipped by stopPolicy.scheduleSegmentBoundaryRule has no synthetic following segment or return beyond the reached stop boundary
returnSchedules.foregroundEndRule: freeze combat state, event timers and decision timers at the exact boundary; do not resolve a partial fixed step
returnSchedules.offlineEndRule: offline.settlement is the sole atomic owner of base credit, guarded known-floor re-clear, its reward sum, one purchase-policy loop and recomputed U; clockModel never repeats any of those steps. After its one compare-and-swap commit, create and evaluate exactly one offline Dawn checkpoint, then dispatch only through postSettlementAttemptEntryRule
returnSchedules.foregroundInterruptionResumeRule: at each foreground segment end persist system.frozenForegroundContext as either null or exactly {contextKind,durablePhase,remainingMs,owningCompletedDawnCount,owningFloor,owningFloorAttemptOrdinal,sourceStateRevision,transactionDraft}, where contextKind is active-combat, wave-gap, defeat-presentation, blocking-post-clear-boundary, blocking-other-decision, or floor-transition; remainingMs, owningCompletedDawnCount and owningFloorAttemptOrdinal are nonnegative safe integers, owningFloor is an integer from 1 through 100, and transactionDraft contains the byte-exact uncommitted timers/events and, for a post-clear boundary, every staged delta under clockModel.postClearDraftRevisionRule while externally visible gameplay run/profile fields remain at the boundary-base snapshot. The hide transaction that persists a non-null context and pending offline event is one shared CAS; its post-hide r+1 is both context.sourceStateRevision and pending.sourceStateRevision. On return, active-combat or wave-gap permits offline settlement immediately and then follows postSettlementAttemptEntryRule; only a byte-identical still-valid owning attempt may resume. A blocking-other-decision completes its one already-open decision transaction before settlement. Special case: timingTargets.f1TutorialDecisionCommit's accepted tap, A1 floorAttemptStart and survival.mandatoryOneHitGateTiming are one interruption-atomic transaction. On a gate pass, that commit replaces the context with active-combat, owningCompletedDawnCount=current profile.completedDawnCount, owningFloor=1 and owningFloorAttemptOrdinal=1, with pendingInitialTutorialGuard=false and exactly one forced guard request/spawn preserved. On a gate rejection, it replaces the context with defeat-presentation for the same owner, preserves pendingInitialTutorialGuard=true, and preserves helperRequestOrdinal=helperSpawnOrdinal=combatEventOrdinal=0. Settlement then either resumes that exact A1-owned branch or invalidates it through postSettlementAttemptEntryRule, and A2 is never created merely by return. A floor-transition follows floorTransitionInterruptionRule as its sole owner. A blocking-post-clear-boundary and defeat-presentation follow deferredOfflineSettlementBoundaryRule and then postSettlementAttemptEntryRule. Only a final completed or cancelled context atomically sets frozenForegroundContext to null; no timer, purchase, Dawn checkpoint, transition, retry, suggestion or choice may execute twice
returnSchedules.floorTransitionInterruptionRule: when hiding during the quantized transition after clearing source floor s<100, keep run.currentFloor=s and persist contextKind=floor-transition with owningFloor=s, owningFloorAttemptOrdinal equal to the just-cleared attempt ordinal, remainingMs, and transactionDraft.transitionTargetFloor=s+1. On return complete exactly remainingMs first with no party/armament selection and no floor-entry Dawn checkpoint. At delay completion, before offline settlement, one CAS applies combatRules.nextFloorCommit by setting run.currentFloor=transitionTargetFloor, sets remainingMs=0 and durablePhase=transition-complete-awaiting-settlement, rewrites context.owningFloor to transitionTargetFloor while retaining owningFloorAttemptOrdinal, and rebases both context and pending event source revisions; this commit creates no attempt. Then execute the one pending offline settlement and numbered offline Dawn checkpoint and call postSettlementAttemptEntryRule. If Dawn or compressed re-clear changes the target floor/Dawn/attempt identity, the context is stale and the ordinary stale branch owns entry. If identity remains exact, clear the transition context and run the null non-Dawn entry suffix exactly once for transitionTargetFloor: preserve party/HP, evaluate armament once, create and evaluate one floor-entry Dawn checkpoint, and either start one attempt or use dawn.reset.postExecutionF1EntryRule if that checkpoint executes Dawn. Never apply nextFloorCommit after settlement, never run a pre-settlement target-floor checkpoint, and never create two target-floor attempts

returnSchedules.deferredSettlementClockRule: on a legal return read returnWallClockUnixMs exactly once and derive frozen monotonicReturnBaseMs and capped elapsedSeconds before any deferred foreground resume. returnSchedules.interruptionDurablePhaseRule: durablePhase begins frozen and advances by compare-and-swap only through the context-applicable subsequence of boundary-committed-awaiting-settlement, retry-prepared-awaiting-suggestion-probe, retry-probed-awaiting-settlement, settlement-committed-awaiting-context-validation, settlement-committed-awaiting-original-checkpoint, settlement-committed-awaiting-failure-resolution, awaiting-result-floor-entry, awaiting-transition, and complete. retry-probed-awaiting-settlement stores whether no legal suggestion existed or the exact held suggestion whose record/achievement commit rebased both pending/context source revisions. returnSchedules.offlineResumeCombatRecompositionRule: when an immediate offline settlement leaves the same active-combat or wave-gap frozen context alive, apply all committed purchase effects to that exact context before resume. returnSchedules.deferredResumeConsumesFollowingForegroun: when an offline segment ends with a deferred frozen context, open the following declared foreground segment and consume resumedForegroundMs one-for-one from the beginning of that segment before any ordinary foreground work; ordinary foreground receives exactly declaredSegmentMs-resumedForegroundMs and the day remains exactly dayLengthSeconds. stopPolicy.successCondition: latch immutable success and completion timestamp at the atomic F100 core clear after reward, highest-floor, first-clear/boss/achievement ledger and profile-U writes, before postgame presentation
stopPolicy.economyTransactionCountingRule: count floor-reward credits, purchase commits, player/policy-selected new shop placement commits, shop reconfiguration commits, offline settlement commits and Dawn commits. Restoring an already retained commercial blueprint at its re-cleared slot is bounded state restoration, not a selected new placement and counts zero economy transactions in both foreground post-clear and compressed offline re-clear. A subtransaction staged inside clockModel.postClearDraftRevisionRule or offline.settlement still consumes its normal economy count and retains its own log even though the containing atomic persistence increments stateRevision only once. Fixed-step live-income accrual, including a step that converts its fraction into one or more whole coins, is deterministic in-memory clock accrual rather than a standalone persisted transaction: do not count it, do not increment stateRevision for it and persist its resulting coins/fraction only inside the next otherwise-authorized transaction. It never triggers a purchase by itself
stopPolicy.combatEventCountingRule: count each unique melee impact, projectile launch, projectile impact or expiry, heal, helper spawn or expiry, delivery arrival, enemy caster event, telegraph, KO and wave or phase transition; same-timestamp batching does not merge their unique event IDs. Shield/charge state mutations are counted only through shieldAndChargeEventCountingRule
stopPolicy.stopCounterLifecycleRule: system.committedEconomyCount and system.committedCombatEventCount are nonnegative safe integers initialized to 0 at the start of each authoritative scenario and are scenario-lifetime monotonic counters. Increment only for events/transactions that commit to that authoritative scenario under economyTransactionCountingRule and combatEventCountingRule; stage nested increments inside their owning atomic draft/clone and expose them only when that commit succeeds. CAS failure, rejected preflight and discarded draft expose no increment. Retry, floor entry, hide/return, offline settlement boundaries and Dawn preserve both counters exactly and never reset them. Every non-mutating effective-power/reference/utility/choice/armament/Dawn-secondary/drift/counterfactual probe clone leaves the authoritative counters untouched and instead receives two isolated clone-local counters initialized to 0 with the same maximumEconomyTransactions and maximumCombatEvents; a clone exceeding either local maximum fails that option/probe exactly as its caller declares, and its local counts never propagate back. Each calibration or holdout scenario is a distinct authoritative scenario and therefore starts both counters at 0. No diagnostic clone inherits the source's already consumed count and no authoritative commit may use a diagnostic local count
stopPolicy.shieldAndChargeEventCountingRule: arming, refreshing, replacing or consuming a Mugi charge, frontline-guard charge, stored helper conversion charge or helper.guard shield is a state mutation embedded in its owning skill trigger, incoming damage event, helper spawn, projectile launch or delivery-work event and creates zero additional combat events, zero additional global IDs and zero emission indices. A frontline-guard activation may arm protectedHitCount charges but adds no event beyond any independently counted owning trigger; each incoming damage event may consume at most one applicable Mugi charge and one applicable frontline-guard charge but the damage event is counted once. Partial or full helper.guard shield absorption is part of that one damage event and shield depletion creates no event. Full-queue conversion with no spawn creates zero combat events. A direct manual guard spawn that consumes one stored guard charge and arms its shield counts exactly one helper-spawn event; a slinger launch consuming its stored charge counts exactly one projectile-launch event; runner charge consumption against delivery work creates no extra event beyond any delivery arrivals actually produced. These mutations remain inside the same atomic preflight even though their additional event cardinality is zero
stopPolicy.sameTimestampCombatLimitPreflightRule: before mutating the real state at timestamp t, clone it and execute the complete simultaneousEventOrder on the clone through a deterministic fixed point, including every same-timestamp nested helper spawn/expiry, shield/charge state mutation, delivery arrival, projectile launch or legal expiry, heal, caster, telegraph, KO and wave/phase transition produced by earlier categories. Future-timestamp events may be scheduled on the clone but are not counted until their own resolution timestamp. Count every event that would commit at t exactly once through combatEventCountingRule and shieldAndChargeEventCountingRule, including generated events that did not exist before the batch. If committedCombatEventCount+exactBatchCount exceeds maximumCombatEvents, discard the clone, mutate no state/carry/counter/ordinal/event queue, commit none of t and stop incomplete. If the legal clone does not clear the final wave/phase, atomically replace the real state with it and add exactBatchCount; equality to the inclusive maximum is legal. Sole exception: if the clone authorizes a final floor clear through mutualZeroResolutionRule, do not replace real state or increment the authoritative count yet; pass the pre-batch real state as boundaryBaseGameplay plus the fully resolved clone and exactFinalBatchCount to clockModel.postClearDraftRevisionRule, which stages and either commits or rolls back the whole final batch with the post-clear suffix. A nested generator may not bypass this clone preflight and neither an ordinary batch nor a final-clear draft is ever trimmed or partially committed
stopPolicy.playerInputCombatLimitPreflightRule: before an accepted manual command mutates state after its timestamp's combat batch, clone the complete post-batch state and execute that one input through helperBaselines.autoDispatch.manualCommandRule and combatRules.helperLifecycle.manualDispatch to a fixed point. Count only the same-input events declared by combatEventCountingRule and apply shield/charge cardinality exactly through shieldAndChargeEventCountingRule. If committedCombatEventCount+exactInputEventCount exceeds maximumCombatEvents, discard the clone, do not count the contact, do not change adaptive carries, request/spawn/combat ordinals, queue, live helpers, stored charges, shields or command anchors, and stop incomplete. Otherwise atomically adopt the clone and count every generated event; equality is legal. Enqueue-only and full-queue conversion inputs may have zero counted combat events but still commit their normal non-event state when within all other limits
stopPolicy.scheduleSegmentBoundaryRule: Step 2/3 authoritative scenario execution alone applies this rule before every declared foreground or offline segment; the five non-mutating consumers named by clockModel.diagnosticHorizonClockRule use their own local horizons instead, and runtime absence is governed only by offline.capSeconds and never by maximumWallClockSeconds. Let remainingWallMs=maximumWallClockSeconds*1000-scenario.resultWallElapsedMs and remainingForegroundMs=maximumForegroundSeconds*1000-scenario.resultForegroundElapsedMs, each required to be a nonnegative safe integer; clockModel.scenarioMeasurementClockRule and clockModel.foregroundProgressionTime are the sole metric mappings. If remainingWallMs=0, or a requested foreground segment has remainingForegroundMs=0, do not start the segment, do not arm a hide, and after the already-due same-timestamp boundary fixed point stop incomplete unless atomic F100 success latched. Otherwise, for a foreground segment execute only minimum(requestedSegmentMs,remainingWallMs,remainingForegroundMs); a clipped segment ends at the earliest exact inclusive maximum, resolves the full same-timestamp legal fixed point there, creates no later segment, and then stops incomplete unless atomic F100 success latched. For an offline segment, its hide transaction at the legal segment start may arm one pending event normally. If requestedSegmentMs>remainingWallMs, set scenario.resultWallElapsedMs to the exact maximum while still hidden; leave the persisted or diagnostic-clone system.monotonicClockMs at the hide boundary, do not synthesize returnWallClockUnixMs or monotonicReturnTimestampMs, do not run elapsedSeconds, settlement, compressed re-clear, purchase, Dawn, deferred resume or context validation, preserve the armed pending event and frozen context byte-exactly, and stop incomplete. If requestedSegmentMs=remainingWallMs, synthesize the return exactly at the inclusive boundary and allow its complete zero-time return/settlement/Dawn/context fixed point, subject to economy/event limits; no positive foreground suffix may exceed either remaining budget. If requestedSegmentMs<remainingWallMs, return normally. After any legal return, deferredSettlementClockRule preflights its complete positive resumedForegroundMs before mutation: equality to both remaining budgets is legal, while an excess advances only the applicable scenario result clock or clocks to the earliest exact maximum, leaves gameplay system clocks at the last durable state, preserves pending/context there, rolls back the owning uncommitted suffix—including the complete F1-F99 final-clear draft when applicable—and runs no settlement or later action. A segment never earns partial offline credit, never settles only the clipped prefix and never advances any gameplay clock or scenario result clock beyond its applicable maximum
stopPolicy.limitBoundaryRule: all numeric maxima are inclusive. Before starting an attempt, Dawn or ordinary economy transaction, reject it only if its declared count would exceed its maximum. Every foreground/offline schedule segment and deferred return first follows scheduleSegmentBoundaryRule; this rule never overrides its no-return/no-partial-settlement result. A floor-clear transactionDraft follows clockModel.postClearDraftRevisionRule: preflight every nested counted economy unit against committed count plus draftEconomyDelta and the F3 scripted delivery's inseparable three combat arrivals against committed count plus draftCombatEventDelta; on either excess discard the entire draft back to the externally visible boundary-base snapshot. Never expose already-staged reward, purchase, arrival, counter, log or ordinal prefixes. Retained-blueprint restoration contributes zero to draftEconomyDelta; a newly selected placement contributes one. Preflight an offline settlement clone before CAS: its economy count is one settlement plus one for every compressed per-floor reward credit plus one for every internal single-level or bulk purchase commit; retained-blueprint restoration contributes zero. Base offline coin credit is included in the one settlement. If current count plus that exact total exceeds maximumEconomyTransactions, discard the entire clone and stop incomplete; never trim purchases or clears. A Dawn including any branch-node spends counts exactly one Dawn economy transaction, not one per node. Preflight every same-timestamp combat batch only through sameTimestampCombatLimitPreflightRule, including transitively generated same-timestamp events, and every post-batch accepted manual command only through playerInputCombatLimitPreflightRule. A transaction, batch or input that lands exactly on a count maximum commits fully, and the scenario may continue until another counted unit is required. Wall-clock and foreground clocks advance only to their exact maxima; resolve every event already scheduled exactly at that boundary in simultaneousEventOrder, including atomic F100 success, but schedule or resolve nothing later. If an F1-F99 final-wave/phase kill occurs in that boundary batch, or an earlier F1-F99 final kill opens a post-clear draft whose required positive-time suffix cannot complete its final boundary CAS at or before both inclusive maxima, clockModel.postClearDraftRevisionRule discards the entire transactionDraft to boundaryBaseGameplay: the final kill, final-batch event count, HP/EHP, queue, reward, logs and ordinals do not commit. The terminal result records the exact reached clock maximum separately and stops incomplete. A suffix that completes at the exact maximum may still run all remaining same-timestamp zero-time actions and commit atomically there. F100 is the sole override: if its atomic core success latches in the exact boundary batch it wins without requiring a post-clear suffix. Otherwise reaching either time maximum stops incomplete after the legal non-clear batch. Never partially commit a purchase, Dawn, floor-clear draft, offline settlement, same-timestamp combat batch or manual input to fit a limit
stopPolicy.floor100TerminalRule: F100's terminal core remains subject to sameTimestampCombatLimitPreflightRule and clockModel.postClearDraftRevisionRule: its final combat batch must fit maximumCombatEvents and its mandatory floor-reward credit must fit as exactly one economy transaction before success can latch. If either preflight rejects, roll back to the pre-final-batch state and stop incomplete; F100's exception covers only the positive-time/generic post-clear suffix, never a combat event, reward, U write or economy count. Once success is latched, simulation time and completion metrics stop; skip old-run free reconfiguration, purchase evaluation and Dawn evaluation. A postgame completion record or UI may read the frozen state but cannot mutate the measured scenario or replace success with a reset. The only non-gameplay exceptions are dawn.branchSpendPolicy.secondaryBranchEarlyTerminalRule and acceptance.activeToPassiveEarlyTerminalRule: each may pad only its discarded clone's diagnosticElapsedWallMs and diagnosticElapsedForegroundMs to its exact comparison horizon while every gameplay field, system clock and completion metric remains byte-frozen

Toto's nonfinal-wave heal uses roundSixDecimals(target maximumHp*waveHealMaxHpFractionInitial) as base-heal. periodic-party-heal uses roundSixDecimals(source cat maximumHp*healOwnMaxHpFraction) as each target's base-heal. effectComposition.relicStackComposition: for each relic family sum baseEffect * relicModel.stackFactorsByOrdinal[instanceOrdinal-1] across owned instances, then treat that family sum as one additive source group before the declared multiplicative order
effectComposition.maximumHpMutationRule: when a persistent transaction changes an alive actor's maximum HP, set current HP to roundSixDecimals(newMaximumHp * oldCurrentHp / oldMaximumHp), capped to the new maximum; a KO actor remains at zero; a newly unlocked actor starts at full maximum HP
effectComposition.outgoingAtomicDamageMechanicBindings: outgoingAtomicDamageOrder is exhaustive and every listed slot is applied exactly once, using identity multiplier 1 when ineligible. encounter-delivery-modifier is exactly one of: enemyModel.firstDistrictMechanics enemy.sack_mole's delivery factor when its exact scope matches; floorOverrides.10.firstDistrictBossMechanics.phaseTwo.landingWindows factor when its exact scope matches; or identity 1. Those two mechanics are mutually exclusive. stored-projectile-charge is the launch-time snapshot carried by a helper.slinger projectile after exactly one stored charge is consumed, otherwise 1. impact-time-helper-rally is the helper-rally multiplier active at the actual helper melee/projectile impact, including a projectile launched before rally activation, otherwise 1. A charged helper.slinger projectile impacting during rally therefore multiplies the stored charge once and then the active rally once before scenario execution power and the sole final roundSixDecimals
effectComposition.projectileDamageSnapshotRule: for every allied projectile launch, after locking its target evaluate the complete declared namedCatAttackOrder or helperAttackOrder against the launch-time committed source/build/shop/support/relic/Dawn/catch-up/seal/tier/armament state and store the resulting finite unrounded launchSourceDamage on the projectile correlation record. Never recompute any of those source slots at impact, so a later source KO/helper expiry, offline purchase, maximum-HP recomposition or other persistent mutation cannot alter an in-flight projectile. Also snapshot the source's skill ID/config and retain a projectile-owned reference to its impact-counter ledger until every already-launched projectile resolves; do not increment a counter at launch. At legal impact, against the immutable locked target and impact pre-commit EHP, evaluate and commit skill-primary-hit exactly once using that retained ledger, so consecutive-hit, every-N-hit, low-EHP and chain eligibility remain impact-owned; an expiry commits none of those counters. Then apply encounter-delivery-modifier from the impact's locked target/delivery and active phase rule, the immutable launch-time stored-projectile-charge, the actual impact-time helper-rally, and the scenario-execution-power multiplier, in outgoingAtomicDamageOrder, followed by the sole roundSixDecimals. Source stats/config are launch snapshots; target EHP, impact-owned skill counters, encounter scope, rally and impact legality are impact-time reads. No other slot may be snapshotted, reapplied or omitted
effectComposition.incomingAtomicDamageMechanicBindings: incomingAtomicDamageOrder is exhaustive and every multiplier slot is applied exactly once, using identity 1 when ineligible. event-class-multiplier is the declared normal, normal-projectile, elite-heavy or boss-heavy event multiplier. owned-charge-multiplier is exactly one of enemy.spark_gecko's consumed 1.35 charge, F10 phase-three's consumed fire-charge multiplier, or identity 1; those owners cannot coexist in one reachable event. phase-execution-multiplier is F100 phase-four phaseFourBerserkDamageMultiplier while that phase is active, otherwise 1. Thus an elite heavy with a gecko charge applies elite class then gecko once; an F10 boss heavy with fire charge applies boss-heavy class then fire once; an F100 phase-four boss event applies its event class then berserk once. No charge or phase multiplier replaces an event-class multiplier
effectComposition.enemyProjectileDamageSnapshotRule: for every enemy projectile launch with a living locked target, evaluate incomingAtomicDamageOrder launch-owned operands enemy-base-hit-and-floor-role, event-class-multiplier and phase-execution-multiplier from the launch-time committed enemy/wave/phase state and store them separately as finite unrounded launchEnemyBaseDamage, launchEventClassMultiplier and launchPhaseExecutionMultiplier. Do not select or consume an owned charge and do not mutate target mitigation, conditional charges or shield at launch. Also store the immutable source actor key, reserved attack kind and generation/slot, event class, phase identity, locked target, due timestamp and correlation key. At a legal impact, never recompute those launch-owned operands: first reserve and consume the then-current eligible source-owned charge through finiteChargeAndCounterReservation, using identity 1 if an earlier melee/heavy consumed it or its owner was defeated, then read the locked living target's then-current committed shop-and-support suppression and armament incoming multiplier and reserve and consume at most one eligible Mugi charge and one frontline-guard charge from the impact pre-commit state. Multiply launchEventClassMultiplier, the impact-time owned-charge multiplier, launchPhaseExecutionMultiplier and every target-side mitigation multiplier; clamp that complete composed multiplier exactly once to incomingDamageMultiplierMinimum; multiply launchEnemyBaseDamage by it, apply the sole roundSixDecimals, then absorb with the target's then-current helper.guard shield HP. If the target is KO, expired or absent, expire for zero damage and consume no source-owned charge, target-side conditional charge or shield. Thus an offline defensive purchase during flight affects the later impact; launch-time source/base/class/phase values do not change, but charge eligibility is deliberately impact-time. No source or target slot may be snapshotted, consumed, reapplied or omitted at any other time
effectComposition.incomingConditionalMitigationRule: Mugi's shield-next-heavy-hit and frontline-guard are finite multiplicative damage reductions reserved before calculation; multiply them with all always-on incoming multipliers, clamp that composed multiplier once to incomingDamageMultiplierMinimum, multiply raw event damage and roundSixDecimals once. A helper.guard shield is not a multiplier and then absorbs from that rounded post-mitigation damage; do not clamp or round again before subtracting exact shield excess from actor HP
effectComposition.secondaryDamageRule: derive chain or splash damage once from the already rounded final primary damage times the declared secondary fraction, roundSixDecimals once, select and lock its target only through combatRules.secondaryTargetRule, and never reapply source, threat, armament, skill, helper-rally or scenario multipliers
effectComposition.effectivePowerReferenceFloorRule: use the explicitly supplied comparison floor when a caller names one; otherwise use run.currentFloor when it is 1 through 100, or floor 100 after scenario completion
effectComposition.effectivePowerReferenceTrace: clone persistent and run state without mutating it; reset transient timers/actors as floorAttemptStart but intentionally preserve each already-selected named cat's exact source current HP after prior recovery/purchase mutation; a newly selected cat has the HP assigned by partySelectionHpTransaction, and initial/Dawn/retry sources are already full by their own rules. Remove live helpers/queues, zero attack/skill cursors and helper dispatch-weight carries, and use the selected build/persona; set trace-local foreground clock/manual-command anchor to 0 so command windows begin at one canonical phase independent of source wall clock. Flatten the reference floor's ordered waves or phases into consecutive horizon segments whose integer durations are largest-remainder allocations of effectivePowerEvaluationHorizonSeconds*1000 by wave/phase EHP share, ties earlier. Every intermediate segment is the half-open interval [segmentStartMs,segmentEndMs): an old-segment event due exactly at that intermediate boundary does not resolve there. The final segment is closed at the exact trace horizon: execute the complete simultaneousEventOrder fixed point for every event due exactly at horizonMs, include its damage/healing/KO in all metrics, schedule or resolve nothing later, and only then sample the endpoint. At first and every later segment start apply that wave/phase's ordinary entry composition and mechanic initialization, including boss gates, F100 phase-three shop lockdown/maximum-HP recomposition and F100 phase-four berserk, while suppressing only the reference-disabled durable log/reward/clear/gap. Initialize enemy EHP and run its repeated reservoir only through effectivePowerReferenceEnemyReservoirRule, use initial alive-enemy count throughout, run exact outgoing/incoming/healing/helper/projectile/heavy/caster streams, and perform every intermediate segment boundary only through effectivePowerReferenceSegmentBoundaryRule. Purchases, coins, income, rewards, unlocks, clears, choices, reconfiguration and Dawn are disabled
effectComposition.effectivePowerReferenceEnemyReservoirRul: at each reference segment start construct that wave/phase's complete exact initial enemy EHP state by the normal floor rules: ordinary F1-F9 firstDistrictEntityEhpAllocation matrix cells and identical backing threat buckets, F8 namedObjectiveWaveEntities and their backing buckets, F10/F100 persistent boss bucket cells, or later aggregate buckets, including the selected F9 variant's exact mechanic owners. Resolve normal entity/bucket target priority, current-to-initial EHP ratios, low-ehp-execute, primary/secondary damage and every owned mechanic against a mutable copy exactly as combat does while maintaining firstDistrictEntityEhpAllocation.invariant. When and only when every entity cell and backing bucket in that complete state reaches zero after one same-timestamp atomic commit, record no durable enemy KO, wave/phase clear, representative gate, reward, recovery, gap or transition; after all effects of that commit and before the next timestamp, replace the entire mutable enemy EHP state with an exact copy of the same segment-initial state, including the same owner identities. This reference-only no-KO rule overrides firstDistrictMechanics.lifecycleRule: an entity/bucket at temporary zero is ineligible for targeting and any due owner event applies its normal positive-EHP predicate and may resolve as a no-op, but its segment-initial owner's pending/future cadence is never cancelled; it continues from the existing due/resolution anchors and becomes effective again after a complete-state refill. Do not reset or cancel attack-kind generations, target carries, attack/skill/helper/caster cadence, status or counters at this virtual refill; ordinary per-hit counter changes caused by the just-committed impacts remain. An individual empty entity/bucket stays zero and target priority moves to another positive target until the whole state refills. No epsilon clamp, infinite EHP, dummy target, bucket-only substitute or mid-segment actor/timer reset is legal
effectComposition.effectivePowerReferenceSegmentBoundaryRu: this rule applies only to an intermediate boundary, never the final trace horizon. At exact segmentEndMs, before any event whose due timestamp equals that boundary, cancel every old-segment pending allied melee shell, allied projectile-launch shell, in-flight allied projectile and secondary event; cancel every enemy normal shell, in-flight projectile, caster, heavy, telegraph and enemy-owned status-expiry event. A cancelled event consumes no hit counter, skill-hit counter, attack-kind slot, target carry step or new combat-event ordinal. Apply the old wave/phase's ordinary exit composition and the next wave/phase's ordinary entry composition at this same boundary, including removing or entering F100 phase-three shop lockdown, recomposing every living named-cat/helper maximum HP and current HP only through maximumHpMutationRule, and entering F100 phase-four berserk; initialize all next-phase gates/mechanics exactly as live combat. Suppress only the gap, durable phase-transition log/event, recovery, reward and clear. For F100 phase 2 to 3, after old-event cancellation enter phaseThreeShopLockdown, recompose HP, caps and command state, then schedule the new segment's allied shells from the carried readiness under the shop-free composition; its phase-entry representative resolves before any new outgoing event. For F100 phase 3 to 4, first apply phase-three exit restoration and maximumHpMutationRule, then activate phaseFourBerserk, then discard all carried enemy cadence and rebuild the first normal event through normalAttackScheduleRule from the new phase start using phaseFourBerserkNormalIntervalMultiplier, and rebuild the first heavy from bossHeavyFirstImpactMs with later recurrences using phaseFourBerserkHeavyIntervalMultiplier; apply phaseFourBerserkDamageMultiplier through the normal incoming slot. These F100 orders override the generic next-segment cadence initialization. Clear old enemy EHP, statuses, mechanic owners, charges, counters, attack-kind generation/cursor and every enemy targeting carry, then initialize the next segment's complete state at the same timestamp. Preserve each named cat's exact recomposed HP, KO state, finite self-owned defensive charge, interval-skill nextDueMs or control/rally latch, and impact-owned skill counters; preserve each live helper's exact recomposed HP, absolute expiry timestamp, stored projectile state only when it is not attached to a cancelled projectile, helper-rally status and helper dispatch-weight carry. First expire any helper whose absolute expiryTimestamp is <=segmentEndMs. For every remaining living named cat or helper clear actorFocusTargetKey and allied target state; carry only whether its attack cooldown would be ready by the boundary. Schedule one new targetless first-contact shell with a new global event ID at segmentEndMs+effectiveContactTravelMs when ready, otherwise at maximum(the old pending shell due timestamp,segmentEndMs+effectiveContactTravelMs); this reference-only reschedule neither resolves nor increments a hit counter at the boundary. Skill timers keep their absolute due timestamps: defensive/healing due exactly at the boundary resolve in the new segment, while a carried control/rally latch releases once under waveGapSkillLifecycle at the new segment's first active fixed tick. Reset no named-cat skill counter unless that skill's ordinary target-reset condition observes the cleared focus. There is no wave gap, recovery, reward, KO, clear or durable phase-transition event, and even a persistent boss actor key cannot carry a projectile or locked target across this boundary
effectComposition.effectiveOutgoingDpsDefinition: sum the full final roundSixDecimals requested outgoing primary and secondary damage value of every committed reference-trace event, including named cats and helpers, before capping subtraction to the target's remaining EHP; overkill never transfers to another bucket but its source event's full final value remains in this diagnostic numerator. Divide by exactly effectivePowerEvaluationHorizonSeconds. Attacks after all selected named cats are KO contribute zero even if a helper lifetime remains
effectComposition.predictedTtkSecondsDefinition: reference floor total EHP divided by maximum(decisionPolicies.purchase.ratioEpsilon,effectiveOutgoingDps); a non-finite result fails the scenario
effectComposition.collapseSecondsForScalarDefinition: the first quantized timestamp in seconds at which any selected named cat becomes KO in the reference trace; if none collapses use effectivePowerNoCollapseSentinelSeconds
effectComposition.survivalMarginScalar: if at least one selected named cat is alive at the end of the reference trace, return the minimum current-HP/max-HP ratio across only those living selected cats, which is strictly positive; if every selected named cat is KO, return negative maximum(decisionPolicies.purchase.ratioEpsilon,(effectivePowerEvaluationHorizonSeconds-lastNamedCatKoSeconds)/effectivePowerEvaluationHorizonSeconds); larger is always better and sign alone defines survive versus fail
effectComposition.effectivePowerScalar: maximum(decisionPolicies.purchase.ratioEpsilon, effectiveOutgoingDps * clamp(collapseSecondsForScalar / maximum(decisionPolicies.purchase.ratioEpsilon, predictedTtkSeconds), 0, 1)); evaluate all named intermediate scalars only through effectivePowerReferenceTrace
effectComposition.armamentRawSurvivalProcedure: for each compared family run its state-faithful effectivePowerReferenceTrace first; set diagnostic horizon=min(90000,ceil(predictedTtkSeconds*1000/fixedStepMs)*fixedStepMs) and replay the exact source-current-HP state through that horizon. armamentDecisionSurvivalOutcome passes only if oneHitCheck passes and at least one selected named cat is alive then; never test survival at 90s when predicted TTK is earlier. Separately make a normalized diagnostic clone with every selected named cat at full composed maximum HP and replay the same family/floor/horizon/keyed draws. On that normalized clone, per actor baseMaxHp is composed maximum HP; healingDuringFight is legal requested healing after non-armament effects but before armament multiplier/capacity; incomingDamageMultiplier is always-on shop/support/relic/armament mitigation clamped to the minimum and excludes conditional charges; predictedRawIncomingDamage is raw targeted event damage after floor-role/event multipliers and before mitigation. Evaluate both formula IDs per actor; family armamentRawSurvivalMargin is the minimum actor margin, tie canonical actor ID. Label it full-condition raw margin. It is secondary to state-faithful survival and never replaces one-hit or live clear/fail

utilityCategoryDefinitions.survival: run effectivePowerReferenceTrace with its trace horizon replaced by utilityProjectionWindowSeconds and all other reference rules unchanged; pass the first quantized KO timestamp in milliseconds of any selected named cat, or null when no selected cat becomes KO, to utilitySurvivalFormulaId. effectComposition.utilityCategoryEvaluationRule: clone the pre-candidate state, calculate all four category values before and after exactly one candidate transaction with purchases, Dawn, unlocks and rewards disabled inside the projection, then pass those eight positive scalars to the purchase utility formula
effectComposition.boundedDecisionProjectionProcedure: under clockModel.diagnosticHorizonClockRule, for each shop-placement, shop-reconfiguration or relic option create two clones of the identical pre-choice state: an unmodified control and a candidate clone receiving exactly that one option. On both clones freeze combat, floor, enemy, helper-delivery work, unlock, reward, Dawn, armament, party and all later shop/relic choices for utilityProjectionWindowSeconds; accrue foreground live income by shopModel.liveIncomeAccrual for the same fixed steps and full local 300000ms horizon regardless of authoritative scenario time remaining; invoke one normal purchase-policy evaluation at the end with cat/helper/levels of already placed shops as its only candidates. Give both clones the same synthetic purchaseEvaluationOrdinal equal to source purchaseEvaluationOrdinal+1 and identical keyed draws without mutating the source. Evaluate both endpoints' effectivePowerScalar and four utility categories against the same explicit reference floor; the projection cannot call itself. The candidate score compares projected candidate endpoint to projected control endpoint, never to an instantaneous pre-choice value
effectComposition.boundedDecisionReferenceFloorRule: a commercial placement or relic choice inside a floor-clear commit uses minimum(100,clearedFloor+1); a failure reconfiguration uses the failed run.currentFloor; a district-boss-clear free-period reconfiguration uses minimum(100,clearedBossFloor+1); pass this explicit floor to effectivePowerReferenceFloorRule for both candidate and control clones
effectComposition.choiceScoreRule: feed the selected build's four purchaseUtilityWeights, control-clone categories as before, candidate-clone categories as after, and waitSeconds=0 to choiceScoreFormulaId; reject non-finite scores; mandatory shop/relic choices rank every finite score even when nonpositive, while optional reconfiguration commits only a score strictly greater than 0; rank by greatest score, then greatest candidate effectivePowerScalar minus control effectivePowerScalar, then each decision's declared stable tie rules
effectComposition.commerceMarginalPowerRule: use boundedDecisionProjectionProcedure and compare its ending effectivePowerScalar to the unmodified clone

districtProgression.districtSealRule: after first clearing district bosses 1 through 9 atomically add one stack to profile.districtSealStacks and mirror it to run.districtSealStacks, never more than districtSealMaximumStacksBeforeFloor100; the floor-100 boss adds no stack

districtProgression.commercialSlotRule: after clearing each placementRelativeFloors slot, first look up that absolute floor in profile.retainedShopBlueprint; if present and the run placement is absent, restore exactly that shop ID at level 0 and never invoke shopPlacement or a first-time choice; if no profile entry has ever been selected, invoke decisionPolicies.shopPlacement once, and the simulation chooses before the next boundary while runtime may defer without opening it; foreground and compressed known-floor re-clear use this identical rule

8.namedObjectiveAllocationRule: replace, never add to, the generic threat-EHP allocation for wave 3. Every withinWaveEhpShare field must be in (0,1], its field value multiplied by 1000000 must be a positive safe integer called the micro-share, and all listed micro-shares must sum to exactly 1000000. Convert the already roundSixDecimals wave-3 EHP to a nonnegative integer micro-EHP with roundHalfUpNonnegative(wave3Ehp*1000000); in listed order allocate each entity except the final one roundHalfUpNonnegative(waveMicroEhp*withinWaveEhpShare), and allocate the final listed entity the exact nonnegative residual waveMicroEhp minus all earlier allocated micro-EHP. Divide each allocation by 1000000 for stored EHP. Derive each backing threat total by summing the stored entity EHP whose threat equals that bucket; an absent bucket has zero, and the entity plus backing totals therefore equal wave-3 EHP exactly in micro-EHP arithmetic. Damage to a named entity decrements that entity EHP and its identical derived backing threat EHP once, not twice
8.objectiveEventCommit: record each named entity's first zero-EHP commit timestamp; atomically add objectiveSuccessEventId at ko-and-wave-clear only when elite.ledger_owl timestamp is strictly less than both other timestamps, treating an entity not yet KO as positive-infinity. A same-timestamp KO tie fails the objective regardless of event enumeration order; the set entry persists even if the remaining floor attempt later fails

reinforcementReservation.attemptStateInitialization: at wave-3 start set successfulArrivals=0, pendingArrival=null, targetInitialEhp to the named allocation, targetCurrentEhp to its carried named EHP, initialWaveArmorEhp to the exact backing armor-bucket EHP, and originalDeliveryRequiredWorkMs to the current delivery's declared initial work when one exists
reinforcementReservation.castRule: at firstCastMs and then repeatIntervalMs from each final cast resolution, if caster EHP is positive, successfulArrivals is below maximum and no arrival is pending, schedule exactly one arrival at cast-resolution+arrivalDelayMs; otherwise the cast makes no pending arrival. Kohaku may delay a cast once under backline-interrupt; the delayed resolution anchors the next cast
reinforcementReservation.arrivalRule: at arrival use combatRules.positiveEhpDeltaReservation. Require the same active wave and require post-damage caster EHP to remain positive. Set reservedRestore=roundSixDecimals(minimum(targetInitialEhp-preCommitTargetEhp,initialWaveEhp*restoreInitialWaveEhpFraction)), allowing a target already at zero before the timestamp to revive; never include same-timestamp new damage in the missing-EHP operand. Add that exact reservedRestore once to the named reserveTarget and once to its identical backing armor aggregate in the atomic EHP commit. Increment successfulArrivals only when reservedRestore is positive. Only on that successful arrival, if deliveryWorkRemainingMs is non-null, add deliveryWorkDelayPerSuccessfulArrivalMs capped at originalDeliveryRequiredWorkMs+deliveryWorkDelayCapMs
reinforcementReservation.sameTimestampCancellation: cast and arrival effects are provisional enemy-non-damage-caster events; compute post-damage caster EHP from preCommitCasterEhp-summedOutgoingDamageToCaster, and if it is zero discard the cast/arrival before every restore, counter or delivery-work mutation. If it remains positive, reserve and atomically combine the arrival with same-timestamp outgoing damage through combatRules.positiveEhpDeltaReservation. A caster KO at any earlier timestamp cancels pending arrival and every future cast; target KO alone does not cancel a pending arrival
